proof.candidate_loss: L=-log(sum of predicted probabilities for the observed allowed outcome set)
proof.construction: For every one-minute allowed set, neither is present. Set the predicted probability of neither to 1 and the probabilities of long-first and short-first to 0. Then the sum on every set is 1 and every loss is 0; a softmax can approach this limit.
proof.consequence: This naive partial-set loss has a degenerate no-hit solution and cannot establish calibrated one-minute first-hit probabilities from these labels alone. The ambiguity is outcome-dependent; excluding it does not fix unconditional probability estimation.
proof.five_minute_imbalance: 16230 of 17288 parents have known neither-side hit at this horizon and research hurdle. A flat no-hit predictor can dominate plain class accuracy; neither is not automatically a FLAT trading action.

candidate_next_design: Retain observed endpoint direction as a separate task, and evaluate magnitude using a predeclared distributional bps representation rather than assuming the already unsuccessful signed-mean auxiliary is sufficient.
Treat first-hit and adverse-path uncertainty explicitly; use a loss only after its observation mechanism, identifiability and nondegenerate baselines are demonstrated.
Fix horizons, costs, class handling and chronological baselines before any comparison; no threshold selected from the current outcomes.
